question.text: The Aland [Oh-land]Islands, a Swedish-speaking archipelago forming an autonomous region of Finland, are found in this gulf, the northernmost arm of the Baltic Sea. This gulf separates Finland and Sweden.
question.clue: To the west of Finland is this gulf and northernmost arm of the Baltic Sea. It contains the Aland Islands and serves to separate Finland and Sweden.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Gaza Strip.
swap.text: In 1993, Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization signed a series of accords named for this city, the capital of Norway. The accords gave Palestinians the right to self-government in Gaza.
swap.clue: Gardermoen airport is the main one serving this city, where the exploration ship Fram and the Kon-Tiki raft can both be visited at museums.

question.text: This Northern European country had its neutrality broken when it was sold out to the Nazis by the traitor Vidkun Quisling.
question.clue: In 1905, it elected Prince Carl as its king, breaking up a union that had been forced since the Treaty of Kiel.

swap.text: The goal of Scott's expedition was to be the first men to reach the South Pole. When they arrived, however, they were devastated to learn that a crew led by this Norwegian had beaten them to it by four weeks.
swap.clue: This Norwegian explorer sailed the Fram to Antarctica in a 1911 expedition that was the first to reach the South Pole, beating Robert Falcon Scott's by one month. This explorer and Scott now co-name an American research station at the South Pole.

question.leadin: The Mannerheim Line was a defensive fortification during this conflict in which "Molotov cocktails" were first used.
question.text: Name this 1939-1940 "seasonal" conflict during which the Soviet Union attempted to invade Finland.
question.clue: Those clashes at Taipale and Summa are not as well known as the Battle of Raate Road, where one side used a decisive ambush; that was part of the larger Battle of Suomussalmi.

swap.text: This war between Finland and the Soviet Union resumed when Finland joined Germany in Operation Barbarossa and became the only democracy to fight with the Axis in World War II.
swap.clue: After serving as prime minister during an earlier conflict, Risto Ryti served as president during this conflict, in which one side aimed to annex East Karelia.

question.leadin: Answer the following about explorers who may or may not have discovered the New World.
question.text: This Icelandic explorer is the first known European to have set foot on continental North America. His visit to "Vinland" has been tentatively identified with the archaeological site of L'Anse aux ["LAN sow"] Meadows in Newfoundland.
question.clue: This explorer earned the nickname "Lucky" after rescuing a shipwrecked crew.

swap.leadin: This man died a year after successfully invading England.
swap.text: Name this Viking father of Cnut the Great.
swap.clue: He divorced his first wife, the daughter of Duke Mieszko of Poland, and on the advice of his second he arranged an alliance that resulted in his great naval victory at the Battle of Svolde.

question.leadin: This leader brought meatballs to his kingdom after trying kofte during his exile.
question.text: Name this king who was joined by Ivan Mazepa in his retreat to Ottoman Moldavia. This king was carried on a stretcher to Turkey due to a foot wound that forced Count Rehnskjold ("RAIN-scold") to lead troops.
question.clue: In Estonia, eight thousand five hundred troops led by Carl Gustav Rehnskiold who assisted this ruler defeated thirty-seven troops led by Charles Eugene de Croy at one battle.

swap.leadin: To flout a Prussian ban on this flag, farmers bred a so-called "protest pig" whose coloration was meant to resemble it.
swap.text: Name this national flag. After a prayer by Archbishop Anders Sunesen, this flag supposedly fell from the sky during the 1219 Battle of Lyndanisse ("lin-duh-NISS-uh").

question.leadin: Answer the following about weird deaths.
question.text: This Danish scientist and author of Introduction to the New Astronomy died after contracting a kidney ailment that was brought on by a banquet in which he refused to leave the table to relieve himself so as to avoid committing a social faux pas.
question.clue: This scientist who constructed the Uraniborg observatory as Lord of Hven. He wore a brass nose after losing a duel.

swap.text: The Battle of Dybbol in the Second Schleswig War took place in this region which makes up most of modern-day Denmark. John Jellicoe led British forces at an inconclusive World War I naval battle named for this body of land.
swap.clue: Admiral Jellicoe's greatest triumph came at this May 31, 1916, naval engagement that saw the defeat of the German fleet under Reinhard Scheer.

question.leadin: A member of this royal family reportedly did not get along with her tutor Rene Descartes, who may have caught pneumonia from teaching her in a cold castle at 5 AM.
question.text: Name this royal family that included a queen who converted to Catholicism and was nicknamed the "Minerva of the North." Axel Oxenstierna ("ook-sen-SHWANN-ah") advised members of this family.
question.answerHtml: House of Vasa [or Vasaätten; accept answers pointing to Vasa Clarke]
question.clue: A queen from this house, who secretly converted to Catholicism, is one of the few women buried in the Vatican Grotto and was nicknamed the Minerva of the North.

swap.text: This European country was the first to introduce banknotes in 1661, replacing the riksdaler. Banks were first chartered under the orders of this country's Vasa dynasty, whose members included Gustavus Adolphus.
swap.clue: This nation was home to a supposed lover of Marie Antoinette, Axel Fersen, who was killed after the overthrow of this nation's ruler Gustav IV.

question.text: The second False Dmitriy lost many of his supporters after the intervention of Sigismund III of the Poland-Lithuania Commonwealth, who used the confusion of the Time of Troubles as an attempt to conquer parts of Russia. Sigismund belonged to this royal house, founded after Gustav I revolted against Christian II and the Kalmar Union.
question.clue: A queen from this royal house abdicated after converting to Catholicism and housed Descartes in his final years.

swap.text: The Cape York meteorite provided iron for the skraeling natives of this island, which also contains the largest-known deposit of free telluric iron. Europeans abandoned the Western and Eastern settlements on this island.
swap.clue: Henrik Kauffman signed a 1941 treaty with the United States paving the way for the establishment of Thule Airbase on this island.

question.text: In this early battle of the Winter War, Russian troops on the Raate and Juntusranta roads were easy prey for defenders under Colonel Hjalmar Siilasvuo. Of the 44,000 in the Russian 44th, only 5,000 made it back to Russia.
question.clue: The earlier Winter War saw the Finns decisively beat the Russians nearby the Gulf of Bothnia at this battle. Hjalmar Sililasvuo led Finnish forces here, defeating General Alexey Vinogradov and General Ivan Dashitsev.

swap.leadin: Rudiger von der Goltz described women combatants in this war by stating "Hardly have the French attacked as fiercely."
swap.text: The Jager ("YAY-ger") Battalion supported one side in what war's Battle of Antrea, which has been compared to Verdun? This conflict over a newly independent former Grand Duchy was followed by "Kinship Wars" with an eastern neighbor.
swap.answerHtml: Finnish Civil War [or Suomen sisällissota or Finska inbördeskriget; accept vapaussota; accept Citizen War or Class War or Red Rebellion; prompt on Civil War or War of Independence]
swap.clue: Veterans of this conflict launched the Aunus and Vien as part of the "Kinship Wars" in nearby countries.

question.text: During the Thirty Years war the Heilbronn League was an anti-Catholic French-Swedish effort led by this Swedish First Minister.
question.clue: This man corresponded extensively with the Dutch merchant Samuel Blommaert ("BLOM-art") to set up a New World colony with his country's "South Company."

swap.text: The Finnish-German alliance did not stay intact, and in this 1944-45 war, Germany decided to secure Petsamo while their 20th Mountain Army got consistently owned in the namesake geographical region.
swap.clue: After signing an armistice with the Soviet Union in 1944, Finland fought this war in order to expel German troops from its territory.
